### p4b
*2026-09-01 14:46*

> what does "guarded seams" mean

Deploy is green and live. The gate flagged two `miso_server` processes writing the same state dir — a residual to fix now. Checking which is which:

**Boundaries are live** — build 411 deployed, gate green all three passes, stamped shipped on everyone's sheet. The map now draws the Sevenoaks constituency as a brighter dashed edge with the 26 district ward lines inside it, and ward names that place themselves so they never overlap — more appear as you zoom. One truth worth Tara knowing: a few *district* wards sit outside the *constituency* line (they really do — different boundaries), so lines outside the dashed edge are correct, not a bug.

**"Guarded seams"** — plain answer: a *seam* is a deliberate joining point one feature leaves for another to plug into (here, the map's `sync` function, which runs after every repaint). *Guarded* means the plug checks its socket exists before using it — the boundaries code asks "is the map feature actually present?" and quietly does nothing if not. That's what lets you untick the map, or the boundaries, and have nothing break: each side survives the other's absence.

**Offsite video storage** — my assessment (not building yet): you're right to wonder. The mini has finite disk, and canvassing video is the one thing that grows without bound — a Saturday of 50 clips at ~30MB is 1.5GB/day. What I'd do: ship Saturday's video with sane recording caps (a couple of minutes per clip, compressed), keep bytes on the mini's exchange blob store for now, and build the store behind a seam so an offsite backend can slot in later. For offsite, the honest options are S3-compatible object storage (Backblaze B2 is ~$6/TB/month and the least lock-in; Cloudflare R2 has free egress) with the mini keeping recent blobs as a cache. That's a proper node with its own ask when you want it — say the word and I'll brief it. Worth noting the transcription design already helps: the *words* travel and get indexed; the heavy bytes stay lazy, so offsite storage doesn't slow the app.

**One ruling for you** (the handover flagged it, and today it got urgent): the CARTO dark tiles now stamp **"API KEY REQUIRED"** diagonally across the live map — it's on every phone today and it's the ugliest thing on the Saturday surface. The fix is one env var (`MISO_TILE_URL`). Options: get a free CARTO API key (keeps the dark look, needs you to sign up), or I point it at plain OSM tiles now (works instantly, but bright — against the dark doctrine). I can flip to OSM as a stopgap the moment you say, or wire in a CARTO key if you get one.

The other three workers (make-posts, QR invite, reports) are still building — I caught one rig writing the live state dir and had it move to its own; otherwise all quiet and healthy.

> ## What shipped
> 
> **`features/miso/users/invite/qr`** — commit `06dcbf6`, cited to `transcripts/2026-09-01-saturday.md#p2`.
> 
> On the invite tool a **show a QR code** pill fills the screen with a code. The person at the door scans it, lands on `/join?t=…`, sees "*_ash invited you*", types their own name and number, gets their text, types the code, and is in the app. The canvasser types nothing.
> 
> **Server** (`qr.rs`, 5 routes on the `route` chain — this node is newest so it is outermost and sees requests before `/gate`): `mint`/`revoke` behind `invite_may` (`authority_rank ≥ 2`); `join`, `check`, `claim` behind a live token only, each stating its own gate. Token = 16 bytes of urandom, hex, one live row per inviter in `~/.miso-auth/invite-qr.json` (temp-write, `0600`, rename; JSON-null = "do not write"), pruned of expired rows on every mint so it cannot fill.
> 
> **Security, as reasoned:** 24h expiry, 25-claim cap, 2s between claims, all server-side; minting fresh replaces the row so the old code dies instantly; the code dies with the inviter's rank or guest-list entry; the token is never logged whole. **A number already on the list gets a byte-identical `{"ok":true}`** — the typed route's "they're already on the list" would turn a leaked code into a membership oracle for the campaign. `_` names refused on this road for anyone (`/pretend` lets an *admin* type one; nobody should mint one by scanning). What a leaked code *can* do: put name/number pairs on the guest list up to the cap, who then become members — the same power the canvasser is deliberately exercising. Named residual: **nothing bounds it per network address — `request` reads `cf-connecting-ip` only for `tunnel` and throws it away.** The canvasser sees the count and taps *new code*.
> 
> **Page:** `qr.js`/`qr.css` (sheet, capture-phase click ownership, SVG drawn from the matrix), `qr.head.html` (one `&lt;script defer&gt;`), `assets/qrlib.js` (qrcode-generator 1.4.4, MIT, vendored unmodified, sha256 `18ae399f…`), `assets/join.html` (the stranger's page, carrying its own phone→code login so the number is typed once).
> 
> **Parent touched, minimally:** `invite.rs` gained `invite_shape_ok(name, phone)` — the three shape rules lifted verbatim out of `invite_add` in the same order, so the claim road obeys exactly the same ones. Proved behaviour-identical with `/qr` unticked.
>

### p8
*2026-09-01 15:35*

> for the QR code invite - I was thinking, what if the workflow was: you type just the user name, we flash up a QR code that goes to a coded link (containing the user details somehow) that's valid for a short time (same as the PIN code), then if a device goes to that URL, we log that user/device as logged in on that device, and we're done. No SMS details or challenge needed.

It works, and the trust model is actually sound — but there's one structural snag worth deciding before I build it. My assessment:

**Why it's sound:** the SMS challenge exists to prove "this person controls this number". At a doorstep you have something stronger — the person is physically in front of you, and you're showing the code to *them*. A five-minute, single-use bearer link (same window as the PIN, which is 5 minutes) minted for one named person is a face-to-face handshake; interception means someone photographing your screen at the door within minutes and burning the token before your visitor does, which the "already used — get a fresh one" path makes visible. For this use, that's fine.

**The snag: miso has no phone-less identity today.** Every account is keyed by its number — `phone:+447…` *is* the world key: it's how cards sync between devices, how push notifications find you, how the exchange knows whose blobs are whose. A name-only user needs a synthetic key (say `user:<random>`), which is buildable, but it changes what the key means in a few places, and it has two real costs:

1. **No recovery road.** With no number, their logged-in device *is* the account. First login auto-enrols Face ID, which helps, but lose the phone before that and the account is orphaned — the canvasser just re-invites, losing whatever they'd posted.
2. **No SMS reach.** You can't text them a login code for a second device later.

**My recommendation:** build exactly your flow — name only, per-person QR, 5-minute single-use token, visiting it logs that device in, done — and let the *number be optional, addable later*: a quiet "add your number" row on their own 👤 card that upgrades the account to a phone key (one server-side migration of their world key), unlocking recovery and second devices. Canvassing gets the zero-friction version on Saturday; nobody is permanently locked into a number-less account.

Also worth keeping: the shipped scan-and-type-your-own-number flow still exists behind the same tool, so if someone *wants* the durable version at the door, it's there.

Want me to build it that way? The key-migration piece is the only part with any depth — I'd brief it as one node (instant-QR) plus one node (add-your-number later, possibly parked until asked).

### p9
*2026-09-01 15:38*

> that makes sense. question though: once a device is logged in, surely we don't need the SMS details for notifications to work?

Correct — notifications don't touch SMS at all. Push goes through web push: at first login the device subscribes via the browser (`pushManager.subscribe` with our VAPID key) and the server files that subscription under the user's world key. The delivery road is the push subscription; the phone number is just the *label* it's filed under today, because the number happens to be the world key. With a synthetic key like `user:<random>`, subscriptions get filed under that key instead and notifications work identically.

So after your instant-QR flow, a number-less user gets everything: sync between the surfaces on that device, push notifications, the works. The number's *only* remaining value is what I named — logging in on a **second** device (the SMS code is how a new device proves who it is) and **recovery** if the phone is lost before Face ID enrolment. Day-to-day, nothing needs it.

That actually simplifies my recommendation: build your flow exactly as you described, and "add your number later" becomes a genuinely optional convenience for people who want a second device — not a prerequisite for anything. Shall I brief it?

### p11
*2026-09-01 15:41*

> while that runs, let's think about offsite video storage options

Let me ground this in the actual numbers first — how much room the mini has and where blobs live today:

Good news first: **this isn't urgent.** The mini has 59GB free, and with the 60-second cap a clip runs 5–10MB — a heavy Saturday (say 6 canvassers × 30 clips) is ~1.5GB. That's a month-plus of hard canvassing before the disk feels it. So we can pick well rather than fast.

**The architecture matters more than the vendor.** What I'd build, whenever we build it:

- The mini stays the **hot cache and front door** — the app never talks to the cloud. The existing blob route is the extensible function: a background uploader pushes each blob to an offsite bucket, verifies the checksum, and only then may the local copy be evicted (oldest-first, once disk crosses a threshold). Playing an old video pulls it back through the same route, invisibly.
- **Encrypt on the mini before upload**, with the key staying on the mini. Doorstep video of residents is personal data (your fieldnote-era GDPR archaeology says take this seriously) — the cloud should hold ciphertext it can't read, in a UK/EU region regardless.
- **Deletion propagates**: a tombstoned post deletes its offsite blob too, so "delete" keeps meaning delete.
- Transcripts and the search index stay local — the heavy bytes are the only thing that travels.

**Vendors, honestly compared:**

| Option | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Backblaze B2** | ~$6/TB/month | S3-compatible, EU region available, boring and reliable — my pick |
| **Cloudflare R2** | ~$15/TB/month, zero egress fees | Free 10GB tier covers the campaign for months; good second choice |
| AWS S3 | ~$23/TB + egress charges | Overkill and priciest |
| Hetzner Storage Box | ~€4/TB | Cheapest but SFTP not S3 — clunkier to integrate |
| USB drive on the mini | ~£50 one-off | Solves *space*, not *offsite* — fire/theft still loses everything |

At campaign scale the bill is pennies either way — a whole year of canvassing video is maybe 50–100GB, so under £1/month on B2. The real choice is "whose account do you want to hold" more than price.

**My recommendation:** B2, EU region, mini-side encryption, built as one node after Saturday (the uploader + eviction + fetch-back behind the blob route, with the encryption in it from day one — retrofitting encryption after plaintext blobs exist offsite is exactly the kind of mess the ledger warns about). If you'd rather stay in one ecosystem you already use, R2's free tier makes it effectively £0 for the campaign's life.

Want me to park it as a named node for next week, or is there a reason to have it before Saturday?

Here's the walkthrough as it'll be on your phone once it takes build 421:

**Open the posts tool** (the bubble). With no post open, the toolbar is now one capture row: **‹ back · 📷 photo · 🎥 video · ● record · + write · undo** — undo last, as always, and everything wearing the posts tool's colour.

**The four roads:**

1. **📷 Photo** — opens the camera/picker. Choose or take a picture and the post is made and *opens ready to type*, caret already in the words — so "photo + caption" is tap, snap, type, done. The picture is shrunk on the phone before it travels.

2. **🎥 Video** — a viewfinder appears; record up to **60 seconds** (the cap is there so a clip can never jam the wire); tap stop. The post appears with a player on it, and the *spoken words from the clip fill themselves in* as the phone finishes transcribing — same whisper path as voice notes. The video bytes go to your own blob store; the words travel and get indexed.

3. **● Record** (audio) — unchanged from what you know: tap, talk, tap stop; the post lands at the top with its words arriving moments later.

4. **+ Write** — a blank post ready to type, title and words.

**Everything after is a post like any other**: title over the photo, delete with undo, EXIF/recording time ordering it among the right day's posts, a pin on the map if it knows where it was, and manual save throughout — the save pill or tapping away, never autosave.

**Two things to expect on first use**: iOS will ask camera and microphone permission once each, on the first tap of 📷 / 🎥 / ● — that prompt path is the one thing the rig genuinely couldn't test, so if a button seems to do nothing the first time, check whether a permission sheet is waiting. And a real multi-MB clip over mobile data is the other untested edge — the upload happens in the background and retries, but you'll be the first to try it on 4G at a doorstep.

To get the update: the usual lozenge on the panel. Live build is **421** — everything above plus today's boundaries, light map, QR invite, and reports is in it.

> **Status:** nothing committed. Worktree fast-forwarded from `5be8a90` to main (`9bdc3f1`) and is clean; baseline `fmlink.py miso` links green (fragments composed: index 205, install 11, login 11, sw 4).
> 
> ### What stopped me
> 
> The brief's tripwire clause: *"If entry-without-phone breaks assumptions too widely (gate, authority, push enrolment filing, `joined` stamping), STOP and contact-report with the list."* It breaks all four, plus card exchange and converge-to-owner.
> 
> The root cause is one fact that the #p8 assessment ("it changes what the key means in a few places") missed: **the identity channel is digits-only, and it is enforced at both ends.**
> 
> - `normalise_phone` (`features/miso/users/users.rs:8`) keeps only `is_ascii_digit` characters. Any hex in a `key` field is silently destroyed.
> - `find_user` and `authority_of` both match by `normalise_phone(entry["phone"])`.
> - Decisively, `/harden` re-checks the guest list *inside token validity*:
> 
> ```rust
> // features/miso/users/harden/harden.rs:43
> !find_user(format!("+{}", parts[0])).is_empty()
> ```
> 
> So a `user:&lt;hex&gt;` account **cannot hold a valid cookie at all** — `token_valid` rejects it on every request. The instant-QR claim route would issue a cookie that dies on its first use. That is not a page-half problem; it is the identity contract.
> 
> ### The map (21 sites, 12 features)
> 
> Twelve sites build the key as `format!("phone:{}", token_phone(t))`; nine strip or test the `phone:` prefix. Two are **semantic, not mechanical** — they would fail silently rather than loudly:
> 
> - `to-owner.rs:28` — `if !who.starts_with("phone:") { return String::new(); }`. A `user:`-keyed world gets **no owner audience**, so converge-to-owner messaging dies for exactly the users this feature creates.
> - `attention.rs:96` — `if format!("phone:{}", parts[3]) != owner`. Push subscription lines are filed under `token_phone`; the comparison rebuilds a `phone:` key and never matches. Attention/present notifications break — which is the property ash specifically asked about at #p9.
> - `exchange_key_of/name_of/audience_of` (`exchange.rs:152,157,166`) all return empty for a phone-less entry, so the minted user is excluded from card exchange entirely.
> 
> Also worth correcting: the brief says "`/by-key` already handles `:`-bearing keys". True but narrower than it reads — `by-key` only lets the localhost `?user=` diag parameter name a raw key. It is not identity resolution and does nothing for this.
> 
> ### The road I recommend (and did not take unilaterally)
> 
> **Keep the key `phone:`-shaped and digits-only; make the digits synthetic.** Mint `+&lt;17+ digits&gt;` — E.164 caps real numbers at 15, so collision with a real phone is impossible by construction.
> 
> Every one of those 21 sites handles an opaque digit string, so authority, push filing, exchange, converge, `joined`-stamping, gate and people **all work untouched**. Ash's actual requirement at #p9 — "a number-less user gets everything" — is satisfied *by construction* rather than by teaching twelve features a second key shape. It also matches the tree's shipped identity glossary (`whole-number.md`: *"identity: the whole-number key for a person, `phone:+&lt;digits&gt;`"*).
> 
> This is not a substitute for ash's ask. Checking the transcript: **`user:&lt;random&gt;` was the main session's own sketch at #p8, never ash's words.** Ash asked for name-only QR onboarding, no phone sharing, working notifications, and a profile slot to add a number later. All four survive this road intact; only the private spelling of the key changes, which the brief hedged as "e.g.".
> 
> Two costs I would need in the re-brief, both fixable inside my two nodes by chain extension:
> 1. `auth_request` would accept the synthetic digits and try to SMS them — must refuse keyless entries.
> 2. The synthetic value sits in the `phone` field, so `invite_invited` and the people card would show a fake number — must be suppressed. (Alternative: store it under a `key` field and chain-extend `find_user`/`authority_of` to resolve it, which keeps `phone` genuinely absent at the cost of two more foreign-function extensions.)
> 
> ### What I need from triage
> 
> A ruling on the key spelling. If synthetic-digits is approved I can build both nodes inside the stated footprint with no foreign file edits. If `user:&lt;hex&gt;` is required, it is a different job — a parent refactor introducing a `token_key()` extension point plus behaviour-preserving edits to 12 features, each needing its own toggle proof, and it should be briefed as such rather than smuggled into two nodes.
> 
> **Open risk, named:** `exchange_audience_of` is `tag(p)` — the last 4 digits. Synthetic ids must not collide there. This is a pre-existing collision surface for real phones too (it is what `/whole-number` was built to fix, and this one site still truncates), so it is worth a look regardless of which road is chosen — I did not verify whether that truncation is load-bearing, so treat it as a hypothesis.</result>
